title: Swan neck dip and lift

source.why_this_clip: A white swan swims slowly to the right across a lake in side view while the camera pans with it; it dips its head and neck toward the water and then lifts its neck upright again by 6.75 s. The clip has no cuts, and this interval holds the one head movement, ending at the last frame.

source_selection.evidence: Builder inspected sixteen raw source frames across the provisional event in preflight-source.jpg; no cut/dissolve observed inside retained interval. Normal-speed playback unrun.

camera.source: phase correlation of consecutive frames on the far bank (rows 0-120: trees and reeds, response 0.99), accumulated and scaled by the far-bank plane depth (5.01) so that plane slides exactly as the bank does in the footage. shots/swan-sam/camera.json (117 px steadily right) was not used: it follows the ripples, which drift right on their own, while the bank shows the camera panning about 33 px and then easing back about 9 px.

planes.label: Trees, reeds and shoreline of the far bank (depth 0.07 vs subject 0.19)
Lake surface: ripples slide with the far bank, because the shot is a pan on a long lens and the measured bank (trees and reeds alike) shows no parallax; the ripples' own drift is not drawn

assembly_summary: Swan glides on the lake with its head held low and then lifts the curved neck near the end while the camera pans. Source and drawing share a fixed 2× viewport crop so the small bird can be inspected.
review_note: Fresh still review v2: native identity met; source framing/pose not met. The source's neck retains a raised forward arch while the head is lowered at 3.75–5.667 seconds, and curls forward again when raised. The drawing instead joins an almost horizontal neck to a sharply hanging tip, then straightens the raised neck and holds the beak nearly level. Recognition classifier, audited final mask fit, four verified contacts and actual normal-speed playback remain unrun or unmet. No training ran.
